name: Bona Fide Visitor Entry / Visitor Extension

requirements.blocker_text: Passport or other appropriate documentation must be valid beyond the date of the return ticket.
Must hold a paid return ticket, or a ticket entitling travel to a next destination outside Antigua and Barbuda.
Must satisfy the immigration officer of sufficient funds to maintain the applicant and any dependants for the period of stay.

outcome.duration_length: up to 6 months on entry, extendable in further periods of up to 6 months (each extension capped at 90 days per application) via the Chief Immigration Officer

sources.title: Immigration Department, Antigua and Barbuda -- Entry and Departure Requirements: documentation, funds, return-ticket rules, up to 6-month initial stay

Immigration Department, Antigua and Barbuda -- Extensions FAQs: 90-day extension cap, in-person application, sponsorship requirement, Immigration and Passport Act 2014's three lawful statuses (visitor, resident, citizen)

notes: NEW COUNTRY, first route of Antigua and Barbuda's initial build. Antigua and Barbuda is a sovereign Commonwealth realm (ISO AG) -- not a British Overseas Territory -- so unlike the four BOTs built earlier this session (Anguilla, Montserrat, Cayman, Bermuda), citizenship here is genuine Antiguan and Barbudan nationality, not a local right-of-abode status plus a separate BOTC track. A 'bona fide visitor' under the Immigration and Passport Act 2014 has no legal right of abode and, per the Extensions FAQ, no automatic right to extend stay merely by holding a work permit -- work permit holders remain classified as visitors for immigration-status purposes even though they may work. No visa-required/visa-exempt nationality list was found in the pages reviewed this pass; modelled as a general entry-and-extension route applicable regardless of nationality, flagged as a gap re: which nationalities require a visa in advance versus visa-on-arrival/visa-exempt entry.
